title: The one who memorized
hookLine: Hafiz of Shiraz (14th century) took his name from knowing the Quran by heart
tomorrow: why do Iranians open Hafiz's book at random?

cards: The memorial is this morning. Zoe has one line to say, and she's afraid she'll freeze reading it off her phone. Inés's grandmother never needed paper: she prayed her rosary by heart, bead by bead.
So, yesterday's question. A Persian poet took his very name from that kind of knowing.

teach.b: His given name was Shams al-Din Muhammad, of Shiraz. The name we know him by is a title.

teach.h: HAFIZ: ONE WHO KEEPS THE QURAN BY HEART.
teach.b: In Muslim communities, a hafiz is someone who has memorized the whole Quran, and the title is an honor. Tradition says he earned it, and his own Divan seems to agree.

teach.h: BY THE QURAN IN YOUR BREAST.
teach.b: In one couplet he talks to himself: I've seen nothing sweeter than your poetry, Hafiz, by the Quran you keep in your breast. He swears by the book he carries inside. That's the teaching under the name.
In Islam, keeping the Quran by heart isn't a party trick.

teach.h: THE WORDS GO WHERE YOU GO.
teach.b: It means the words go where you go, into the dark, into old age, into a room with no book in it. Inés's grandmother had the same kind of treasure: the rosary's prayers, worn smooth by years of saying.
What you hold by heart is there when the paper isn't.

how: In Muslim communities, a hafiz is someone who has memorized the whole Quran; the title is an honor. The poet Hafiz of Shiraz is known by that title as his pen name.

games.q: what does “the one who memorized” mean?
o: a Persian court poet paid to praise the king
a scribe who copied holy books out by hand
a title for someone who knows the Quran by heart

games.q: a week of Rumi, and a new name: tap the pairs.
p: one who keeps the Quran by heart

s: it's a title: one who knows the Quran by heart. his given name was Shams al-Din Muhammad.
'come, come, whoever you are' is a line from Rumi's Masnavi
it's a Persian quatrain about coming back to God, not found in Rumi's books.
Mevlevis call the night Rumi died his wedding night
Sheb-i Arus: the lover meets the Beloved.

games.q: a friend has to give a toast at her sister's wedding and keeps losing her place on her phone. what does the name Hafiz suggest?
o: learn the one line that matters by heart.
read it faster so it's over sooner.
skip the toast; a card says it just as well.
games.why: a hafiz carries the words inside. what you hold by heart is there when the paper, or the phone, isn't.

practice: Choose one line you love: from your own tradition, from this week, or your own four lines. Say it out loud, then again without looking, and again, until it stays. Let the last minute be the line, said quietly, by heart.

wordCard.voice: The one who memorized: hafiz, a title for someone who keeps the whole Quran by heart. A poet of Shiraz made it his name.

orig.note: Arabic and Persian: one who keeps; a person who knows the whole Quran by heart.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: by heart, where the words stay when the paper's gone. A week closed, and Hafiz has begun.
